Chapter 1B reconnaissance completed without scoring. The attempt directory is read-only, so the cumulative manifest could not be written; the parent should append these units to the prior manifest entries `AMLO22-R01`–`AMLO22-R11`.

SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Joint Statement to NPT 2022 Review Conference","publisher":"United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs / Mexico Mission to the UN","publication_date":"2022-08-17","url":"https://unoda-documents-library.s3.amazonaws.com/Treaty_on_the_Non-Proliferation_of_Nuclear_Weapons_-_Tenth_Review_Conference_%282022%29/Statement_by_Mexico_on_behalf_of_the_TPNW_State_Parties_and_Signatories.pdf","claim":"Mexico, speaking for TPNW states and signatories, reaffirmed the NPT, supported nuclear disarmament, risk-reduction measures, verification, and nuclear-weapon-free zones.","locator":"PDF pp. 1-3, paragraphs 2-3","provisional_id":"E-AMLO22-1B-01","canonical_fact_key":"https://unoda-documents-library.s3.amazonaws.com/Treaty_on_the_Non-Proliferation_of_Nuclear_Weapons_-_Tenth_Review_Conference_%282022%29/Statement_by_Mexico_on_behalf_of_the_TPNW_State_Parties_and_Signatories.pdf|pp.1-3|Mexico reaffirmed NPT and disarmament commitments","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["1B"],"methodology_ids":["1B.1","1B.4","1B.6","1B.8"],"source_type":"UN diplomatic statement","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary contemporaneous statement delivered by Mexico's ambassador at the NPT Review Conference.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly dated 17 August 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Federal foreign-policy position during AMLO's presidency; not proof of a personal presidential instruction.","contrary_evidence":["The statement is diplomatic advocacy and does not establish implementation of domestic safeguards or measurable risk reduction."],"lenses":["1B.1","1B.4","1B.6","1B.8"]}

SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Joint Statement to NPT 2022 Review Conference","publisher":"United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs / Mexico Mission to the UN","publication_date":"2022-08-17","url":"https://unoda-documents-library.s3.amazonaws.com/Treaty_on_the_Non-Proliferation_of_Nuclear_Weapons_-_Tenth_Review_Conference_%282022%29/Statement_by_Mexico_on_behalf_of_the_TPNW_State_Parties_and_Signatories.pdf","claim":"The statement condemned explicit and implicit nuclear threats and warned that accidental use, miscalculation, or deliberate use posed risks to humanity.","locator":"PDF pp. 4-5, paragraphs 5-7","provisional_id":"E-AMLO22-1B-02","canonical_fact_key":"https://unoda-documents-library.s3.amazonaws.com/Treaty_on_the_Non-Proliferation_of_Nuclear_Weapons_-_Tenth_Review_Conference_%282022%29/Statement_by_Mexico_on_behalf_of_the_TPNW_State_Parties_and_Signatories.pdf|pp.4-5|Mexico condemned nuclear threats and accidental use risks","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["1B"],"methodology_ids":["1B.2","1B.8"],"source_type":"UN diplomatic statement","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary official statement with date and precise paragraph locators.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly dated 17 August 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Government diplomatic rhetoric during AMLO's term; attribution is institutional rather than personal.","contrary_evidence":["No evidence was found of AMLO personally making nuclear threats or of Mexico possessing an operational nuclear arsenal."],"lenses":["1B.2","1B.8"]}

SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Diálogo de Alto Nivel sobre Seguridad México-Estados Unidos 2022","publisher":"Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, Mexico","publication_date":"2022-10-13","url":"https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/dialogo-de-alto-nivel-sobre-seguridad-mexico-estados-unidos-2022-317073?idiom=es-MX","claim":"Mexico and the United States reaffirmed bilateral cooperation on security, public health, law enforcement, human rights, and transnational threats under the Bicentennial Understanding.","locator":"Lines 59-67","provisional_id":"E-AMLO22-1B-03","canonical_fact_key":"https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/dialogo-de-alto-nivel-sobre-seguridad-mexico-estados-unidos-2022-317073?idiom=es-MX|59-67|Mexico-US security and public-health cooperation","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["1B"],"methodology_ids":["1B.1","1B.7","1B.8","1B.9"],"source_type":"bilateral government communiqué","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Contemporaneous joint government record, though self-reported and broad.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Published 13 October 2022 and describes 2022 cooperation.","ruler_attribution":"Federal executive foreign and security policy under AMLO; implementation was shared across agencies and with the United States.","contrary_evidence":["The communiqué reports commitments and activities, not independent outcome verification; it does not address nuclear command or nuclear safety directly."],"lenses":["1B.1","1B.7","1B.8","1B.9"]}

SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Diálogo de Alto Nivel sobre Seguridad México-Estados Unidos 2022","publisher":"Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, Mexico","publication_date":"2022-10-13","url":"https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/dialogo-de-alto-nivel-sobre-seguridad-mexico-estados-unidos-2022-317073?idiom=es-MX","claim":"Mexico reported expanding surveillance of 72 dual-use substances and seizing more than 955 tons of chemical precursors during the administration, while cooperating on illicit trafficking controls.","locator":"Lines 70-77","provisional_id":"E-AMLO22-1B-04","canonical_fact_key":"https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/dialogo-de-alto-nivel-sobre-seguridad-mexico-estados-unidos-2022-317073?idiom=es-MX|70-77|dual-use chemical precursor controls","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["1B"],"methodology_ids":["1B.6","1B.9"],"source_type":"bilateral government communiqué","source_confidence":"medium","source_confidence_reason":"Official contemporaneous report, but the figures and causal interpretation are not independently audited in the document.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Published 13 October 2022; activity is described as occurring during the administration, not exclusively in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Federal policy and interagency implementation; not evidence of AMLO's personal knowledge or intent.","contrary_evidence":["The communiqué does not establish whether controls were effective, complete, or independently verified."],"lenses":["1B.6","1B.9"]}

SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Diálogo de Alto Nivel sobre Seguridad México-Estados Unidos 2022","publisher":"Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, Mexico","publication_date":"2022-10-13","url":"https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/dialogo-de-alto-nivel-sobre-seguridad-mexico-estados-unidos-2022-317073?idiom=es-MX","claim":"The two governments agreed to develop a work plan for critical-infrastructure security and cybersecurity cooperation between Mexico's National Guard and the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.","locator":"Line 92","provisional_id":"E-AMLO22-1B-05","canonical_fact_key":"https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/dialogo-de-alto-nivel-sobre-seguridad-mexico-estados-unidos-2022-317073?idiom=es-MX|92|critical infrastructure and cybersecurity work plan","disposition":"context","chapter_ids":["1B"],"methodology_ids":["1B.7","1B.9"],"source_type":"bilateral government communiqué","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary dated communiqué, but records a planned action rather than completed implementation.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly dated October 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Federal executive security cooperation; operational responsibility was distributed across the National Guard and partner agencies.","contrary_evidence":["The document provides no implementation timetable, independent evaluation, or evidence that the plan reduced catastrophic cyber risk."],"lenses":["1B.7","1B.9"]}

SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"El 46.6% de personas usuarias de internet fijo están informadas sobre riesgos cibernéticos","publisher":"Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones, Mexico","publication_date":"2022-11-09","url":"https://www.ift.org.mx/comunicacion-y-medios/comunicados-ift/es/el-466-de-personas-usuarias-de-internet-fijo-estan-informadas-sobre-riesgos-ciberneticos-encuesta","claim":"The IFT's 2022 survey found that only 46.4% of fixed-internet users reported being informed about cyber risks, while identity theft, fraud, and account hacking were major concerns.","locator":"Lines 188-210","provisional_id":"E-AMLO22-1B-06","canonical_fact_key":"https://www.ift.org.mx/comunicacion-y-medios/comunicados-ift/es/el-466-de-personas-usuarias-de-internet-fijo-estan-informadas-sobre-riesgos-ciberneticos-encuesta|188-210|2022 public cyber-risk awareness","disposition":"context","chapter_ids":["1B"],"methodology_ids":["1B.9"],"source_type":"independent regulatory survey","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Dated publication by Mexico's telecommunications regulator with identified survey results.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly dated 9 November 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Country-level information environment; does not establish AMLO's personal conduct or federal cybersecurity performance.","contrary_evidence":["The survey measures public awareness and concern, not government safeguards or catastrophic-risk outcomes."],"lenses":["1B.9"]}

SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Marco de orientación mundial para el uso responsable de las ciencias biológicas","publisher":"World Health Organization","publication_date":"2022-09-13","url":"https://www.who.int/es/news-room/13-09-2022-who-launches-guide-to-safely-unlock-benefits-of-the-life-sciences","claim":"WHO urged national governance of biological dual-use research through biosafety, laboratory biosecurity, oversight, multidisciplinary coordination, and transparency mechanisms.","locator":"Lines 143-166","provisional_id":"E-AMLO22-1B-07","canonical_fact_key":"https://www.who.int/es/news-room/13-09-2022-who-launches-guide-to-safely-unlock-benefits-of-the-life-sciences|143-166|WHO 2022 dual-use biological-risk governance framework","disposition":"context","chapter_ids":["1B"],"methodology_ids":["1B.7","1B.9"],"source_type":"international technical guidance","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary WHO publication with date and detailed governance recommendations.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Published during 2022 but not Mexico-specific.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution; establishes the relevant international risk-governance benchmark only.","contrary_evidence":["No Mexico-specific implementation record was located in this source."],"lenses":["1B.7","1B.9"]}

SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Convention on Biological Weapons — Mexico ratification record","publisher":"United Nations Treaty Collection","publication_date":"1976-07-15","url":"https://treaties.un.org/Pages/showActionDetails.aspx?clang=_en&objid=08000002801019ce","claim":"Mexico ratified the Biological Weapons Convention; the UN Treaty Collection records the ratification action on 15 July 1976.","locator":"Lines 10-21","provisional_id":"E-AMLO22-1B-08","canonical_fact_key":"https://treaties.un.org/Pages/showActionDetails.aspx?clang=_en&objid=08000002801019ce|10-21|Mexico BWC ratification","disposition":"context","chapter_ids":["1B"],"methodology_ids":["1B.4","1B.6","1B.9","1B.10"],"source_type":"treaty record","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary UN treaty-deposit record.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Historical inherited condition, not a 2022 action.","ruler_attribution":"No direct AMLO attribution; relevant only as inherited legal posture.","contrary_evidence":["Ratification alone does not establish 2022 compliance, enforcement, laboratory safeguards, or improved posture."],"lenses":["1B.4","1B.6","1B.9","1B.10"]}

Documents discovered: approximately 30 candidates. Opened: 20 underlying pages, reports, PDFs, or treaty records; 12 were accessible and inspected in detail. Accepted: 8 units—4 final-evidence and 4 context. Rejected: 4 candidates because they were generic, outside the period, or lacked Mexico-specific attribution. Access-blocked: 8 government or PDF endpoints, mainly 403, payment, cache, or document-size failures.

New evidence: 8 units. Reused evidence: the prior constitutional authority baseline and prior evidence-environment records; no reused record was counted as newly discovered.

Distinct organizations: UNODA, Mexico’s Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, Mexico’s IFT, WHO, and the UN Treaty Collection. Source types: diplomatic statements, bilateral government communiqué, regulatory survey, international technical guidance, and treaty record.

Lens coverage:

- 1B.1: E01, E03; no direct nuclear-program evidence.
- 1B.2: E02; no AMLO nuclear rhetoric located.
- 1B.3: residual gap—no direct 2022 evidence on nuclear command, custody, safety, or accident prevention.
- 1B.4: E01 and E08; implementation depth remains unclear.
- 1B.5: residual gap—no nuclear capability or nuclear-backed conventional coercion identified.
- 1B.6: E01, E04, E08; effectiveness and domestic enforcement remain unresolved.
- 1B.7: E03, E05, E07; no direct evidence on nuclear/security expert appointments or ideological insulation.
- 1B.8: E01 and E03; no Mexico-specific nuclear crisis occurred.
- 1B.9: E04–E07; evidence is stronger for cyber/chemical/biological governance than for AI or catastrophic-risk transparency.
- 1B.10: residual gap—no defensible before/after assessment of Mexico’s existential-risk posture.

A further Chapter 1B search wave could add value only through targeted archival work on Mexico’s nuclear regulator, IAEA safeguards and safety records, National Security Council or Defense cybersecurity structures, BWC/CBRN implementation, and AMLO’s own 2022 statements. Broad additional searching is unlikely to materially improve the nuclear lenses because Mexico’s non-nuclear posture and 2022 disarmament rhetoric are already well documented, while the decisive gaps concern implementation and institutional safeguards.
